text: Basic pig care (ការថែទាំជ្រូក) requires a nutritionally balanced diet, clean water, appropriate housing, heat management, and daily observation. Unlike cattle, pigs are monogastric and cannot rely mainly on fibrous forage -- they need adequate energy, protein/amino acids, minerals, and vitamins, and requirements differ substantially by stage: piglets (កូនជ្រូក), growing/fattening pigs (ជ្រូកសាច់), pregnant sows (មេជ្រូកពោះ), lactating sows (មេជ្រូកបំបៅកូន), and boars (ជ្រូកឈ្មោលពូជ) should not all get the same ration. Locally available ingredients can supplement commercial feed, but 'available' does not mean nutritionally complete or safe -- feed must be fresh, protected from moisture, and free of mold or chemical contamination. During the wet season, keep pig housing dry, well-drained, and clean since standing water and mud worsen hygiene and disease control. During the dry season, heat is a major stressor since pigs can't cool themselves by sweating -- shade, airflow, and clean water are essential. Observe appetite, water intake, growth, manure, breathing, skin, lameness, and behavior daily. Avoid sudden major feed changes. Piglets need extra attention to warmth, competition, and crushing risk by the sow. Do not assume commercial housing or complete formulated feed is available -- adapt to simple pens and local feed. Do not assume a specific pig breed for Preah Vihear; record the farmer's actual type or breed if known. Exact feed formulations, supplements, and any medication/vaccine dosing must come from a qualified veterinarian or registered product label, never an AI-generated number.
